sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the glossary page
sections.what: Brings in the tools the page needs: data fetching, the industry context, the card, badge and citation drawer components, and icons for search, book, links, arrows and loading.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: CitationLocator
sections.title: Citation locator shape
sections.what: Describes where inside a source a fact can be found, such as a page or section, with a type and an optional value.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a citation point to the exact place in a source, not just the whole document.
sections.watch_out: The value is optional, so code that reads it must handle a locator that has only a type.

sections.name: Citation
sections.title: Citation record shape
sections.what: Describes a source record with an identifier, title, web address and optional details: source name, publisher, access date, short excerpt and locator. These fields feed the citations shown for glossary terms.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The shape lets every glossary term point to a source in the same way.
sections.watch_out: Most fields are optional, so display code must cope with a citation that is missing its publisher, excerpt or locator.

sections.name: GlossaryTerm
sections.title: Shape of a glossary term
sections.what: Describes one glossary entry as a term, its definition, an optional category, and a list of citations that may be empty or missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: it tells every other part of the page what a term contains.
sections.watch_out: Citations can be null, so any code that reads them must allow for a missing list.

sections.name: NUCLEAR_CATEGORY_ORDER
sections.title: Nuclear category display order
sections.what: Lists the nuclear categories in the order they should appear on the page, with General last.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the nuclear glossary reads in a logical sequence from reactors to organisations.
sections.watch_out: The names must match the category text in the data exactly, or the group falls to the end of the list.

sections.name: LNG_CATEGORY_ORDER
sections.title: LNG category display order
sections.what: Lists the LNG categories in the order they should appear, with General last.
sections.why: Likely reason: same as the nuclear list, so LNG terms follow a sensible reading order.
sections.watch_out: Category names are matched exactly, so a renamed category will be moved to the end without warning.

sections.name: CATEGORY_ICONS
sections.title: Category icons
sections.what: Maps each category name to a symbol shown beside it on the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: a small visual cue helps a reader spot categories quickly. The comment says category names are unique across industries, so one shared map is safe.
sections.watch_out: Two different categories can share one icon, and a new category without an entry shows no icon.

sections.name: CATEGORY_ORDER_BY_INDUSTRY
sections.title: Curated order per industry
sections.what: Connects each industry code to its fixed category order, nuclear and LNG only.
sections.why: Likely reason: industries that have a set order get it, while others use the alphabetical fallback.
sections.watch_out: An industry added here must use the same code as the rest of the app, or its curated order is silently ignored.

sections.name: Glossary (part 1)
sections.title: Loading and searching terms
sections.what: Fetches the glossary for the current industry, fills in default categories and citation titles, and filters terms by the search text in their name or definition.
sections.why: Likely reason: the data from the server is inconsistent, so it is tidied here before the page uses it. Search is kept simple so results update as the visitor types.
sections.watch_out: Fallback citation ids are built from the term name and position, so duplicate term names can produce duplicate ids.

sections.name: Glossary (part 2)
sections.title: Grouping terms by category
sections.what: Sorts the filtered terms into category groups, uses the curated order when one exists, puts leftover categories alphabetically after that, and drops empty groups.
sections.why: Likely reason: so each industry shows its own intended order and new categories still appear.
sections.watch_out: The selected term is found by name, so a duplicate name would select the first match only.

sections.name: Glossary: if
sections.title: Page header and search box
sections.what: Shows a spinner while data loads, then the page title, the total term count, a row of category badges and the search box with a result count.
sections.why: Likely reason: a spinner avoids showing an empty page while data arrives.
sections.watch_out: The count at the top shows all terms, not just the filtered ones, so it will not change during a search.

sections.name: Glossary (part 4)
sections.title: Mobile and wide list layout
sections.what: On small screens shows either the chosen term with a back button or the category list. On wide screens shows the list on the left at all times.
sections.why: Likely reason: a narrow screen cannot fit two panels, so the page shows one at a time.
sections.watch_out: Both layouts use the same selection state, so changing one layout's behaviour can affect the other.

sections.name: Glossary (part 5)
sections.title: Right-hand term detail panel
sections.what: On wide screens, shows the selected term's details beside the list, or a prompt to select a term when none is chosen. Also places the citation drawer and clears its selection on close.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the list and the detail visible together while reading.
sections.watch_out: The panel is sticky, so very tall content may be cut off unless the page scrolls correctly.

sections.name: CategorySection
sections.title: Collapsible category headers
sections.what: Draws a button for each category that shows its icon, name and count, and lists its term cards only when open.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a visitor hide categories they are not reading.
sections.watch_out: Collapsed state is kept in the parent page, so a category stays collapsed during searches even if it has matches.

sections.name: TermCard
sections.title: Single term card
sections.what: Draws one clickable card with the term name, a count of its references and the first two lines of its definition, highlighted when selected.
sections.why: Likely reason: a short preview lets a visitor scan terms before opening one.
sections.watch_out: The card key uses the term name, so two terms with the same name will confuse React and may show wrong highlights.

sections.name: TermDetail
sections.title: Term detail with citations
sections.what: Shows the full term, its category, its definition and a list of sources. Clicking a source opens the citation drawer.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each claim traceable to its sources.
sections.watch_out: The source title falls back to the source name or Untitled, so a missing title may look odd to a reader.

sections.name: EmptyState
sections.title: Empty state messages
sections.what: Shows one message when an industry has no glossary terms yet and a different message when a search finds nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: a visitor should know whether terms are missing or just not matched by the search.
sections.watch_out: The message text is fixed, so a change to how terms are stored may need the messages checked as well.

summary: Reference page that lists the glossary terms for the current industry, grouped by category, with search and a citation viewer for each term.
purpose: Lets a visitor look up standard terms, read their definitions and open the sources behind them.
why: Likely reason: a glossary is easier to scan when terms are grouped by category, and each definition needs sources so a reader can check it.
how: 1. Loads the glossary for the current industry and fills in missing categories and citation titles. 2. Filters terms by search text in the name or definition. 3. Groups them by category, in a fixed order for nuclear and LNG, and alphabetically for other industries. 4. Shows a list and a detail panel, with a different layout for small and wide screens. 5. Opens a citation drawer when a source is clicked.
inputs: The current industry from the industry context, the glossary data from the server, the search text and the chosen term or citation.
outputs: A searchable, grouped list of terms with a detail view and citation drawer. Nothing is saved.
risks: Terms are matched and selected by their name, so two terms with the same name would clash and both would highlight. Citations are given a made-up id when missing, which can repeat if a term name repeats.
debug: If terms are missing, check the glossary response and the category name. If a group is in the wrong place, check the curated order lists for the industry. If citations show as Untitled, check the citation title and source fields in the data.
